title: Week 2 — Legal Rulings, Evidence & Wājib
subtitle: Thawāb · Ḥanafī distinctions · Dalīl · Categories of wājib
description: Explore the consequences of legal rulings, the Ḥanafī classification of obligations and prohibitions, degrees of certainty in legal evidence, and the classifications of wājib.
source: Islamic Legal Theory I – Level One, CICFL, pp. 52–58.

questions.q: 15. Complete the table: for each category, state what happens when the action is performed and when it is not performed. Are thawāb, ʿiqāb, and ʿitāb synonymous?

rows.label: Mubāḥ (permissible)
accepted: no reward no punishment no reprimand
no reward no punishment no reprimand

questions.explanation: The course distinguishes three consequences: thawāb (reward), ʿiqāb (punishment), and ʿitāb (reprimand). They are not synonyms. A wājib is rewarded when performed and its omission is punishable; a mandūb is rewarded when performed and its omission merits reprimand; a muḥarram is punishable when performed and its omission is rewarded; a makrūh merits reprimand when performed and reward when avoided; a mubāḥ entails none of these consequences whether performed or omitted.

questions.q: 16. According to the course, when does a person deserve ʿiqāb (punishment)?
questions.answer: When a person performs a muḥarram act or omits a wājib act.
acceptedAnswers: when a person performs a muharram act or omits a wajib act
performing a forbidden act or failing to perform an obligatory act
when one does a forbidden act or leaves an obligatory act
questions.displayAnswer: Performing a muḥarram act or omitting a wājib act.
questions.explanation: A forbidden act is punished when performed, while an obligatory act is punished when omitted.

questions.q: 17. According to the course, when does a person deserve ʿitāb (reprimand)?
questions.answer: When a person omits a mandūb act or performs a makrūh act.
acceptedAnswers: when a person omits a mandub act or performs a makruh act
omitting a recommended act or doing a disliked act
when one leaves a recommended action or performs a disliked action
questions.displayAnswer: Omitting a mandūb act or performing a makrūh act.
questions.explanation: The course distinguishes reprimand from punishment: omission of a mandūb and performance of a makrūh merit ʿitāb, not ʿiqāb.

questions.q: 18. According to the course, when does a person deserve thawāb (reward)?
questions.answer: By performing a wājib or mandūb act, or by refraining from a muḥarram or makrūh act.
acceptedAnswers: by performing a wajib or mandub act or by refraining from a muharram or makruh act
performing obligatory or recommended acts and avoiding forbidden or disliked acts
when one does a wajib or mandub and leaves a muharram or makruh
questions.displayAnswer: Performing a wājib or mandūb, or refraining from a muḥarram or makrūh.
questions.explanation: The course identifies reward for performing obligatory and recommended acts, and for avoiding forbidden and disliked acts. A mubāḥ action by itself entails no reward, punishment, or reprimand.

questions.q: 19. Are wājib and farḍ synonymous? Give the qualification made in the course.
questions.answer: Yes according to non-Ḥanafī jurists; Ḥanafīs distinguish them: wājib is established by a ẓannī indicator, while farḍ is established by a qaṭʿī indicator.
acceptedAnswers: yes according to non hanafi jurists; hanafis distinguish them
they are synonymous according to the jumhur but not according to hanafis
yes for the jumhur; hanafis distinguish wajib as zanni and fard as qati
questions.displayAnswer: They are synonymous according to non-Ḥanafī jurists. Ḥanafīs distinguish wājib (ẓannī evidence) from farḍ (qaṭʿī evidence).
questions.explanation: Both refer to mandatory acts whose performer deserves reward and whose non-performer deserves punishment. The difference is evidentiary in the Ḥanafī classification.

questions.q: 20. Are makrūh and makrūh tanzīhī synonymous? Explain the distinction in the course.
questions.answer: Not exactly in the Ḥanafī classification: makrūh is divided into makrūh tanzīhī and makrūh taḥrīmī. Makrūh tanzīhī is the disliked act that does not amount to a forbidden act.
acceptedAnswers: no; hanafis divide makruh into makruh tanzihi and makruh tahrimi
not exactly; makruh is the broader category and makruh tanzihi is one subdivision
makruh tanzihi is a subcategory of makruh in the hanafi classification
questions.displayAnswer: Not exactly: in the Ḥanafī classification, makrūh is the broader category, divided into makrūh tanzīhī and makrūh taḥrīmī.
questions.explanation: The course identifies makrūh tanzīhī as a disliked act not amounting to a forbidden act, and makrūh taḥrīmī as a disliked act amounting to a forbidden act. Avoid treating the broad category and one of its subdivisions as exact synonyms in the Ḥanafī taxonomy.

questions.q: 21. Are muḥarram and makrūh taḥrīmī synonymous? Explain the Ḥanafī distinction.
questions.answer: They are synonymous according to non-Ḥanafī jurists, but Ḥanafīs distinguish them: makrūh taḥrīmī is established by a ẓannī indicator, while muḥarram is established by a qaṭʿī indicator.
acceptedAnswers: yes according to non hanafi jurists; hanafis distinguish them
they are synonymous according to the jumhur but hanafis distinguish them by zanni and qati evidence
yes for the jumhur; hanafis distinguish makruh tahrimi as zanni and muharram as qati
questions.displayAnswer: They are synonymous according to non-Ḥanafī jurists. Ḥanafīs distinguish makrūh taḥrīmī (ẓannī evidence) from muḥarram (qaṭʿī evidence).
questions.explanation: Both describe forbidden acts whose performer deserves punishment and whose non-performer deserves reward. The Ḥanafī distinction concerns the strength/certainty of the indicator establishing the prohibition.
